notes: organic mantle during phase A: Courtney -> Tanisha d17

convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Marcus doesn't wait for an answer. "We need to discuss how things are run here."
"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane… That's Nevermore telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"He lowers the crown. That's Rut King telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"We lost Courtney and DeAndre this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check the treeline every hour at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"System, aliens, whatever — the snares still need checking. You can philosophize after the work's done."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Still on the big questions."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Hah. Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"...Anyway. Sorry. What's on your mind? You'd know about that."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't a machinist. I was a mechanic. I weighed the lie against what the truth would cost them. The lie was cheaper."
Aurora looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Aurora rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"We never finished talking about grief — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You're a good listener, you know that? A tired smile.'"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Aurora. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"BROTHERS! That's The Union Rep telling you it's about to move. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"Still on grief."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"That we're interesting to it. Being watched means being kept. I'd rather be boring to the sky. Boring things get left alone."
"Can I be honest? Still on what scares you most."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Courtney is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About that question — Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Hollow Belly. They just... took Reham and Daniyar. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"It crouches low, tail lashing once, twice. That's The Mountain Lord telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Lotus Root. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. Cairo, Egypt in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored."
"Still on what you miss most."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"They took me. Hollow Belly — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I sleep in short shifts. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

identityTrips.text: ◈ THE GRANT — full integration. The System opens the last slot like a door it built just for Courtney. "You have been adequate entertainment. We upgrade adequate." (Ability slots: 6)

deathBeat: d17: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Courtney Buckley is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d17: 🕯️ Courtney Buckley is dead — combat. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d17: The village's quarrel was with Courtney — and Courtney is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d18: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. DeAndre Han is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d18: ◈ CRISIS — THE FIRST GRAVE. DeAndre is dead. The village digs its first grave, and everyone understands at once: this place can kill you. It just did.
recoverHome: d18: That night, they bring Courtney home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d17: At the grave, DeAndre, Aurora, Marcus speak for Tanisha — "Courtney trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d17: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d17: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We have already cleared your morning. You are welcome. We require 300 kcal of tubers and your full attention. The fans love a cooking segment."
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We will keep practicing on our own." You decide, firmly, not to ask what that means.
d18: SYSTEM: "Oh. Oh no. Was that supposed to happen? The audience is crying. I did not know they could do that."
